text:
maria: Rolling out adaptive tail-KV prefetch + latency-aware microbatcher to prod now (10:45 PT). Canary at 5% -> 25% -> 100% if green.

deploy-bot: deploy started: commit e7a1d4f -> prod | canary=5% -> 25% -> 100% | sha e7a1d4f | eta 00:20:00

alex: Pulled the first 30m of metrics from the perf board. Quick headline: p50 -9%, p95 -24%, p99 -19%, cost per 1k tokens -18%. Full numbers below.

alex: ```
baseline: {p50: 90ms, p95: 240ms, p99: 520ms, cost_per_1k: $0.045} 
deploy:   {p50: 82ms, p95: 182ms, p99: 420ms, cost_per_1k: $0.037}
```

jen: nice work. Any difference by model size or request length?

alex: Short requests (<=64 tokens) saw the biggest cost and p95 wins (~25% cost reduction). Medium (65-512) ~15% cost win. Long (>1k) p95 improved ~10% but cost impact smaller.

samir: How does the microbatcher avoid adding latency for low-concurrency paths?

maria: microbatcher uses a latency ceiling (configurable, default 10ms). If the batch wait would exceed ceiling we issue single-request inference. Also it prefers merging requests that share prefix KV lifecycles to maximize cache reuse.

runtime-oncall: Observed a short queue spike during 25% step (~60s) but it subsided. No GPU OOMs. We saw a handful of 429s coming from an older SDK client pinned to v1.12; fallback route handled the rest.

ops: can we add a temporary alert: queue_length > 100 for >90s after rollouts? Create a follow-up ticket.

maria: created ticket INF-8723 and added a hotfix alert rule (PR #4360).

product: can you give a short blurb we can share with customer success? they'd like a one-paragraph note and an FAQ line about long-context workloads.

maria: drafting shareable: "Typical short-context workloads should see ~20-30% lower inference cost and ~20% lower p95 latency. Long-context workloads will see smaller cost wins but lower p99 due to better KV prefetch locality." Will post doc link when ready.

alex: internal perf dashboard: https://internal.redwood/perf/graphs/1792401234 (internal)

samir: can we note the fallback policy tweak in the release notes? That prevented more 429s.

maria: will include a note + changelog entry. Also scheduling a dedicated-pool canary next Wed 09:00 PT to validate reserved capacity behavior under bursty traffic.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: commit e7a1d4f -> prod | status=success | duration=00:26:20 :rocket:

runtime-oncall: continuing to monitor for 48h. will escalate if p99 regresses beyond baseline. thanks team! :tada:
